new="""## A throwing `beforeSession`

- A `beforeSession` that throws fails the turn like any other orchestrator failure: the error still reaches the caller as a rejection, `onError` receives it, and `afterSession` runs ([validated by: runs onError and afterSession when beforeSession throws](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.beforeSession.acceptance.test.ts#L40), [validated by: receives the error a throwing beforeSession raised](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L284)).
- When `afterSession` runs after a throwing `beforeSession`, none of the turn happened: the provider was never called, no tool ran, and the session it receives holds exactly the entries it arrived with ([validated by: hands afterSession an untouched session when beforeSession throws, with the provider never called](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L302)).
- `afterSession` is deliberately not told why it runs: it receives only the session, so it cannot tell a `beforeSession` that failed part-way from a turn that finished. A cleanup in `afterSession` must therefore release only what `beforeSession` actually allocated — record the allocation on something the deployer owns, keyed by `sessionId`, and treat a missing record as nothing to release. A deployer who needs the failure itself reads it in `onError`, which fires before `afterSession`.

## Measured semantics — out of scope
"""
